MECHANISM: Incrementally shorter parameter EMA horizon

HYPOTHESIS: Lowering the EMA decay cap from 0.98 to 0.975 will exceed 9,358 correct predictions by further reducing evaluation-weight lag while retaining smoothing over roughly 40 late-training updates.

INTENDED_EDIT: Reduce only the learned-parameter EMA decay cap from 0.98 to 0.975.

EVIDENCE: Live BatchNorm buffers improved validation correct from 9,345 to 9,351, and reducing the EMA cap from 0.99 to 0.985 and then 0.98 improved it to 9,357 and 9,358. The 0.975 attempts timed out despite having identical computational cost, so this evidence-guided setting remains unresolved.
